S1.problem: Hardsub is a standalone top-level struct in Config. D1.outcome: Implemented end-to-end. Config: PipelineConfig struct with DormancyPeriod field added; Config gains Pipeline field; defaultCFG includes PipelineConfig{DormancyPeriod: 0}. DTO: DormancyPeriod added to Options. Pipeline: struct field added, NewPipeline copies from opts, Run() sleeps dormancyPeriod after each pass when > 0 (cancellable via ctx), falls back to polling ticker when == 0. cmd_process.go: --dormancy flag with fallback to cfg.Pipeline.DormancyPeriod. Tests: TestNewPipeline_DormancyPeriodDefault, TestRun_DormancyMode_SleepsBetweenPasses, TestRun_DormancyMode_ContextCancelledDuringSleep, TestRun_DormancyDisabled_Polling, TestRun_DormancyMode_ContinuesAfterScanFailure.
D1.problem: The cyclic mode polls every 1 second even when the pipeline is idle. There's no concept of 'process once, then rest for N minutes before checking again.'
D1.proposal: Add a configurable dormancy period to cyclic mode: after each scan pass completes (success or failure), sleep for the configured duration before the next pass. Zero value preserves current polling behaviour.
tests: TestNewPipeline_DormancyPeriodDefault — zero value means disabled
TestRun_DormancyMode_SleepsBetweenPasses — verify sleep between passes with fast duration
TestRun_DormancyMode_ContextCancelledDuringSleep — context cancellation during dormancy exits loop
TestRun_DormancyDisabled_Polling — zero dormancy uses polling ticker
TestRun_DormancyMode_ContinuesAfterScanFailure — sleep happens even after failed passes
D1.title: Dormancy period for cyclic mode
trade_offs: Replaces 1-second polling with configurable sleep (backward compatible via zero value)
Minimal config surface: one duration field
